item.title: Adapting to the risk of Atlantic circulation change
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01961-1

Weakening Atlantic circulation could shift temperatures and rainfall across continents, raise regional sea levels, disrupt food production and marine ecosystems, and erode the ocean carbon sink. Planning in the most exposed countries does not yet account for these risks; we propose five steps to close this blind spot.
